newsitem.title: JORDAN: Institutions buoy Jordan market at week's end.
newsitem.headline: Institutions buoy Jordan market at week's end.

text.p: Jordanian shares performed well at end of weekly trade on Wednesday after outside institutional buying emerged on a handful of bluechip firms topped by Arab Bank, brokers said.
"The market was healthy, there was demand by outside buyers on companies which had good profits and plan to raise their capital," said Ibrahim Odeh, a broker in Wataniyeh Financial Services.
Odeh said outside buying appeared to come from institutional investors, global funds and large investors.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.63 percent to 152.55 points, recouping some of its losses which sent the bourse last Sunday to its lowest levels in four months.
Dealers say recent falls have made some blue chip stock attractively priced, drawing some local investors back into the market in bargain hunting.
Turnover was a high 729,881 dinars ($1.03 million) with trade in Arab Bank accounting for most of Wednesday's daily volume after 1,820 shares worth 465,310 dinars changed hands.

The bank, heavily weighted on the official 60-share market index, helped cushion the index after rising 3.50 dinars to 257.50 dinars in trade which brokers said was triggered by active floor trader and outsider demand.
Political uncertainty combined with a lack of liquidity has recently depressed sentiment and prompted outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.

Among a handful of stock which were focus of investor interest were Jordan Selpho Chemicals which rose 0.03 dinars to 0.72 dinars and Jordan Industrial Resources which shed 0.06 dinars to close at 1.17 dinars.
The market on Wednesday saw 17 shares rising while 15 fell. Another 11 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.60 percent to 80.04 points, 4.02 percent down from the start of the year.
